target_task.text: Long-context transformer decoding and efficient key-value (KV) cache memory management.

limitation.text: Massive KV caches create severe memory-bandwidth bottlenecks during long-context decoding, while rigid sparse heuristics drop necessary context and lead to quality degradation.

combination.text: By modifying standard softmax attention training through the multiplicative suppression of sub-threshold logits toward a uniform attention floor, models avoid representation collapse and localized attention sinks on initial tokens. This enables efficient token and block pruning to hard-prune uninformative KV blocks at inference time while preserving critical attention sinks and maintaining dense model quality.

summary.text: This opportunity briefing investigates combining attention sinks, pruning, and softmax for long-context transformer decoding and efficient key-value cache memory management. By modifying standard softmax attention via multiplicative suppression of sub-threshold logits toward a uniform attention floor, models avoid representation collapse and localized initial attention sinks. This mechanism enables effective pruning to hard-prune uninformative KV blocks at inference time while preserving critical anchor tokens and maintaining dense model quality. According to DVF axis scores, Demand is 3.0 and Feasibility is 4.0, while Viability is missing.

target_user.text: The target user is unverified due to a lack of patent assignee data in the bundle, though open-source repositories such as repo:mit-han-lab/duo-attention and repo:sail-sg/attention-sink indicate an audience of machine learning researchers and inference engineers optimizing long-context large language models.

jtbd.text: When deploying large language models on long-context tasks, I want to eliminate memory-bandwidth bottlenecks without suffering quality degradation from rigid sparse heuristics, so that I can achieve hardware-accelerated decoding speeds while preserving critical context.

value_prop.text: Unlike methods that use rigid heuristics to drop context, this combination uses smooth uniform attention floors and dynamic contextual thresholds to allocate dense-like context to difficult retrieval steps while pruning routine tokens. It delivers up to 2.5x wall-clock decode speedups over FlashAttention-2 on sequences up to 512K tokens while rivaling dense attention quality.
